[...] [p. 96] Les exemples présentés ci-dessous démontrent que l’okande est une langue où les tons présentent une fonction distinctive. En effet, le ton [H] et le ton [B] sont en opposition distinctive. Par conséquent, on distingue en okande deux tonèmes : /H/ et /B/. new_statements.translation: [p. 95] It is important to specify that when the /H/ tone is in final position it tends to lower and is thus realised as a mid tone [M]. [p. 96] The examples presented below demonstrate that Okande is a language in which tones have a distinctive function. Indeed, the [H] tone and the [L] tone are in distinctive opposition. Consequently, two tonemes are distinguished in Okande: /H/ and /L/. [p. 102] The analysis of Okande tones allows, at the lexical level, three schemes to be identified for nominal stems (/L/, /LH/ and /HL/). The domain of tone is the nominal stem.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Okande is described as a tone language with two contrastive level tones (H, L) and stem-level lexical melodies; the only phonology chapter available says nothing about word stress or accent (no mention of penultimate prominence, lengthening or intensity). The only positional effect noted is lowering of word-final H to mid, plus an invariably H-toned noun prefix.
new_statements.exceptions: Falling [HB] surface tone only on stems with prenasalised C1 (H prefix + nasal); noun prefix H replaced by L in a few (indefinite) contexts. Author states the tone analysis is preliminary: elderly speakers, transcription from recordings, nouns in citation form only, no post-lexical study.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical level, nouns in isolation (citation forms elicited from Okande speakers resident in Libreville, July 2005); no phrase-level prosody described.
new_statements.identity_note: Grollemund 2006 describes o-kande (Okande, B32, kand1300) from speakers originating in the Boleko / Aschouka / Kongo-Mboumba villages near Booué (Moyen-Ogooué) but recorded in Libreville; same variety as Van der Veen's 1991 sketch (Hombert's ALGAB informants from Boleko and Aschouka). Van der Veen 1991/2003 treats Kande, Pinzi (pinj1243) and Himba (simb1255? 'ɣe-himba', B302) as a Northern-B30 dialect cluster; the tonal statement quoted is specific to Kande, and Grollemund notes Kande's invariable H noun prefix is NOT shared by the other B30 varieties.

sources.locator: Ch. III, 1re partie (Phonologie), §6.2.2 p. 95, §6.3 p. 96 (PDF p. 97), §6.5.7 p. 102
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Ch. III pt 1 sec. VI 'Tons' (pp. 94-104): Okande has two distinctive tonemes /H/ and /B/ (p. 96), lexical noun-stem melodies /B/, /BH/, /HB/; domain of tone = nominal stem (p. 102); word-final /H/ tends to lower to [M] (p. 95); nominal prefix always H (pp. 95, 103ff, analysed as a trace of the augment). Author flags the tone analysis as preliminary (elderly speakers, transcription from recordings, nouns at lexical level only).

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 2003. The B30 language group. In Nurse & Philippson (eds), The Bantu Languages, 371-391. London: Routledge.
sources.note: No stress statement. Sec. 2.2.2 'Tone systems' (p. 380): Tsogo/Vove/Viya have H, L, HL, LH noun melodies; 'No reliable tonal data are available for N-B30 so far' (N-B30 = Pinzi/Kande/Himba cluster). Kande entry pp. 373-374: main publications Guthrie, VdV 1991a 'basic outline based on some 300 lexical items'.
